# Public-health example tables

Sources retrieved on 2026-09-17. Full instructions and figures are in
`dev/public-health/README.md` in the source repository. The source lock is
`data-raw/public-health/sources.json`; rebuild with `prepare.py` in that directory.

Each bacterial dataset has chromosomes.tsv and blocks.tsv for whole-sequence views,
and features.tsv and links.tsv for gene-level views. Whole-sequence units are
kb; gene units are bp. Intervals are zero-based and half-open. `windows.tsv`
records displayed feature spans. `protein_matches.tsv` contains the unfiltered
regional BLASTp output. The plasmid alignment audit contains unfiltered BLASTn
hits and their retention decisions. `sequences.tsv` gives record versions,
lengths, original organism names, source links and sequence hashes.

The **Anopheles** dataset adds `anopheles/chromosomes.tsv` and `blocks.tsv`
for 380 published synteny blocks in two malaria-vector species. Its coordinates
are **block ranks, not base pairs**; sequence sizes count blocks. There are no
Anopheles gene-feature tables. Its original source spreadsheet, signed
permutations, per-arm summary, source lock and checksums are included in that
subdirectory. See [Anopheles methods and attribution](anopheles/README.md).
Rebuild it with `python3 data-raw/public-health/prepare_anopheles.py`.
The source article is CC BY 4.0 and states its data are CC0 unless otherwise
noted; the source spreadsheet is retained unchanged with attribution to Jiang
et al. (2014), doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0459-2.

## Provenance and third-party data

The Bartonella backbone is redistributed from genoPlotR 0.8.11, Lionel Guy,
CRAN mirror commit 3887f91ed718b7df935c11d1a84e9276f4f6b01c:
https://github.com/cran/genoPlotR/blob/3887f91ed718b7df935c11d1a84e9276f4f6b01c/inst/extdata/barto.backbone
The upstream package declares GPL (>= 2). The unchanged source is included at
`data-raw/public-health/sources/barto.backbone` in the source repository.
The derived `bartonella/blocks.tsv` retains that GPL (>= 2) notice; it is not
relicensed under the package's MIT license. A copy of GPL version 2 is supplied
as `GPL-2.0.txt`; later GPL versions may be used as permitted by the upstream
license. Original changes are documented in the preparation script: coordinate
conversion, minimum-length filtering and expansion into genome pairs.

The sequence lengths and gene annotations are derived from the public NCBI
records linked in `sequences.tsv`. Retain attribution to the original
sequencing projects when reusing them. The newly computed plasmid alignments
and regional protein-match tables are generated by the supplied script.

The plasmid biological source is Conlan et al. (2014), Science Translational
Medicine 6:254ra126, doi:10.1126/scitranslmed.3009845:
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4203314/
ECNIH3 retains the historical study label E. cloacae in figures; the downloaded
record identifies it as Enterobacter hormaechei subsp. hoffmannii.

These tables document comparative sequence structure. They do not infer a
patient-to-patient transmission event, resistance phenotype, or clinical action.
